newsitem.title: FRANCE: Vatry multi-modal takes stall at Americas fair.
newsitem.headline: Vatry multi-modal takes stall at Americas fair.

text.p: The French multi-modal freight transport project, Europort Vatry, is making an effort to market itself in the U.S. by taking a stand at the Air Cargo Americas fair in Miami on October 29-31, its marketing director said.

"The Miami fair will be our second "international" event following the International Air Cargo Forum in Dubai last Autumn," Arnaud Southon, marketing director of the semi-public company running the project, SAEM Europort, told Reuters.

"Having a stand at this event is designed to bring us into contact with air cargo users, who are large, U.S. shippers seeking a central hub for distribution in western Europe and forwarding agents, and secondly, transport and logistics providers in the form of cargo airlines and express operators," he said.
SAEM Europort had appointed a firm of American consultants, the Bridge Group, to promote the Vatry project in the U.S., Southon added.
"The Far East is another region we are targeting and have a representative based in Tokyo."

The local public authority, Conseil General de la Marne, is investing one billion francs over the next two years in transforming the ex-NATO airfield into a multi-modal freight platform, incorporating full-freighter flights.
"Our long-term aim is to capture part of long-haul full-freighter traffic handled at European airports estimated at 2.5 million tonnes annually and which is expected to grow by six percent a year."

Development work at the site, which is situated around 150 kilometres east of Paris, began earlier this year and the first operational activities - probably specialising in logistics and surface transport distribution, will probably start-up mid-1998, Southon added.

"Given the major airport infrastructure work required, comprising the construction of a control tower, service buildings and the upgrading of the runway, the first full-freighter flights are unlikely to take place before mid-1999."

Six candidates, grouped into French, international and Franco-international consortia, are to submit bids by September 1 to run the site. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
